sources.fullCitation: “Anläßlich eines Presseempfanges sprach der stellvertretende Produktionschef der Wien-Film Erich von Neusser über das Wiener Filmschaffen” [caption]. Photographs credited “Aufn. Wiener Bühne – Strof.” Die Bühne (Vienna), no. 6, 1940, p. 11. Österreichische Nationalbibliothek / ANNO.
sources.title: Presseempfang der Wien-Film
sources.creator: Strof (photographer)
sources.researchNote: The page carries two photographs of the same occasion. The upper one shows von Neusser speaking, with the chief dramaturge Hans Gustl Kernmayr beside him; the lower one, from which the likeness here is taken, places him next to the actress Hilde Krahl and the director Gustav Ucicky. The caption states the office he then held, deputy head of production of Wien-Film, which no other record gathered for him gives, and dates it to 1940 — seven years after the Viennese film he directed to music by Kaper and Jurmann.

media.title: Erich von Neusser at the Wien-Film press reception — Die Bühne, 1940
media.description: Detail cropped from the lower of two photographs on page 11 of Die Bühne, number 6 of 1940, reporting a press reception at which Erich von Neusser, deputy head of production of Wien-Film, spoke about film-making in Vienna. The full photograph shows, from left to right, von Neusser, the actress Hilde Krahl and the director Gustav Ucicky; the detail is confined to von Neusser, seated with a cigarette over his papers.
media.altText: Dark-haired man in a dark suit seated at a table, smoking, looking down at papers he holds in both hands.
media.rightsNote: The page credits the photograph “Aufn. Wiener Bühne – Strof”, but the photographer’s identity and dates have not been established. ANNO supplies the digitized page without clearing third-party rights in the underlying photograph; reuse therefore requires a separate rights assessment.
media.publicCaption: Erich von Neusser at the press reception at which he spoke on Viennese film-making, in Die Bühne, number 6 of 1940. The full photograph is captioned “Von links nach rechts: Erich von Neusser, Hilde Krahl, Spielleiter Gustav Ucicky.”
